intro: Precision, seasonality and umami: pristine seafood, dashi broth, rice and pickles, from counter omakase to late-night ramen.
flavours: Soy sauce, dashi, miso, mirin, rice, wasabi, nori
hk: Hong Kong is one of the biggest markets outside Japan for Japanese food, from omakase counters to Ichiran and Genki Sushi.

dishes.name: Sushi (nigiri)
dishes.what: Hand-pressed vinegared rice topped with raw fish or seafood.

dishes.name: Sashimi
dishes.what: Thin slices of very fresh raw fish served without rice.

dishes.name: Ramen
dishes.what: Wheat noodles in rich broth: tonkotsu (pork), shoyu, shio or miso, with chashu pork and a soft egg.

dishes.name: Tempura
dishes.what: Seafood and vegetables in an ultra-light, crisp batter, dipped in tentsuyu.

dishes.name: Tonkatsu
dishes.what: Thick breaded pork cutlet fried golden, served with shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce.

dishes.name: Udon
dishes.what: Thick, chewy wheat noodles in a light dashi broth or served cold.

dishes.name: Soba
dishes.what: Thin buckwheat noodles, often served cold on a bamboo tray with dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Yakitori
dishes.what: Chicken skewers grilled over charcoal, seasoned with salt or sweet tare.

dishes.name: Okonomiyaki
dishes.what: Savoury cabbage pancake topped with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and seaweed; Osaka and Hiroshima styles.

dishes.name: Takoyaki
dishes.what: Osaka street snack: balls of batter with octopus inside, cooked in a special pan.

dishes.name: Japanese curry
dishes.what: Thick, mild, slightly sweet curry over rice, often with a katsu cutlet on top.

dishes.name: Gyūdon
dishes.what: Rice bowl topped with thinly sliced beef and onions simmered in sweet soy. Yoshinoya made it famous.

dishes.name: Unadon
dishes.what: Grilled freshwater eel glazed with sweet soy, over rice.

dishes.name: Onigiri
dishes.what: Rice balls wrapped in nori with fillings like salmon or tuna mayo; a convenience-store essential.

dishes.name: Mochi
dishes.what: Soft, chewy rice cake made from pounded glutinous rice, often filled with red bean (daifuku).
